elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly permits Company to terminate the Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part.

elements.element: Customer may terminate on thirty (30) days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires thirty (30) days' advance notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly requires advance written notice.

elements.element: Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees following a convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires Contractor to refund prepaid fees attributable to Services not performed as of termination, substantively providing the unused or pro-rata portion of prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Contractor's convenience right under Section (a) applies only when there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding. Thus, Contractor cannot terminate for convenience while an outstanding committed Statement of Work remains uncompleted; Section (b) is a for-cause right, not a convenience right.
Section (c) expressly grants Company a convenience-termination right covering the Agreement and any Statement of Work.

elements.element: Customer's convenience-termination notice period is between sixty (60) and ninety (90) days.
elements.evidence: Section (c) specifies thirty (30) days' notice, which is more favorable to Company but is outside the fallback's stated 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section (c) permits termination without penalty or early-termination charge, so the applicable fee is zero and therefore below the cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section (a) permits Contractor to terminate whenever no uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding. That trigger is not expressly limited to the end of a term, and the Agreement itself is evergreen under Section 2.

elements.element: Vendor must provide ninety (90) days' notice to terminate for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section (a) requires only fifteen (15) days' advance notice from either party.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Company has a 30-day written convenience-termination right, receives prepaid fees attributable to unperformed Services, and Contractor cannot terminate for convenience while an uncompleted Statement of Work is outstanding. The fallback is not independently satisfied because the customer notice period is not 60–90 days and Contractor retains a 15-day right that is not expressly confined to the end of a term. The redline is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated commercial intent because new Section (b) adds mutual breach-termination rights, payment obligations, and an assignment of works in progress, none of which is necessary to address termination for convenience.
